handshape: Hold your non-dominant hand open as a base, palm facing you. Touch the tip of your dominant index finger to the tip of the base hand's thumb. (Vowel: thumb.)
Bring the thumb tip and index-fingertip of both hands together so the two thumb-and-index circles interlock; keep the other fingers relaxed.
With your dominant hand alone, make an open 'C' shape, as if cupping a can. C is the only BSL fingerspelled letter formed with a single hand — the base hand is not used.
Touch your dominant index fingertip to the tip of the base hand's index finger, and place your dominant thumb tip at the base of the base hand's index finger.
Touch your dominant index fingertip to the tip of the base hand's index finger. (Vowel: index finger.)
Lay the pads of your dominant index and middle fingers across the backs (knuckle bases) of the base hand's index and middle fingers, dominant hand on top.
Clench both hands into fists and stack them on top of each other, resting on their sides, with your dominant fist on top.
Lay the four fingers of your dominant hand flat on the base hand's palm, then slide them downward off the base hand's fingertips in one small movement.
Touch your dominant index fingertip to the tip of the base hand's middle finger. (Vowel: middle finger.)
Start with your dominant index fingertip at the tip of the base hand's middle finger, trace down toward the wrist, then move up to the tip of the base hand's thumb.
Bend your dominant index finger into a hook and press the back of the bent finger against the middle of the base hand's index finger.
Lay the tip of your dominant index finger flat on the base hand's palm near its edge. The flat-laid angle is what distinguishes L from T.
Hold your dominant index, middle and ring fingers together and lay them flat on the base hand's palm.
Hold your dominant index and middle fingers together and lay them on the base hand's palm. Keep the two fingers together or it reads as V.
Touch your dominant index fingertip to the tip of the base hand's ring finger. (Vowel: ring finger.)
Pinch your dominant index finger and thumb together into a small circle and touch the circle to the tip of the base hand's index finger.
Close the base hand's index finger and thumb into a circle, and place the tip of your dominant index finger into the middle of that circle.
Bend your dominant index finger and lay it on the base hand's palm with the fingertip pointing toward the wrist.
Bend your dominant little finger and hook it onto the base hand's little finger, interlocking the two.
Point the tip of your dominant index finger straight down onto the base hand's palm near its edge. The downward angle is what distinguishes T from L.
Touch your dominant index fingertip to the tip of the base hand's little finger. (Vowel: little finger.)
Spread your dominant index and middle fingers into a V shape and lay them on the base hand's palm. The spread distinguishes V from N.
Thread all the fingers of your dominant hand through the gaps between the fingers of the base hand. Use all fingers — index fingers only would read as X.
Lay your dominant index finger across the base hand's index finger so only the two index fingers cross. Using all the fingers would read as W.
Place the tip of your dominant index finger at the join between the base hand's thumb and the rest of the hand.
Hold the fingers of your dominant hand together and place them on the base hand so the dominant hand sticks up at a right angle to it.
